I am 73 years old. I have farmed in Quzhou County on the North China Plain my whole life, and I only finished primary school. I do not need books to tell me what this land wants. Every year I grow winter wheat and summer maize on my 5 mu — that is the rotation that works here, one wheat crop and one corn crop on the same piece of land. My wheat is already in the field from last October; I sowed improved Jimai seed. Now it is spring, and I will topdress it with urea when it greens up, irrigate it three times before early June harvest, and spray four times for weeds, aphids, and rust. I rotary-tilled the field before sowing the wheat. After the wheat comes off, I will plant hybrid Denghai maize straight into the stubble without tilling — that is how we save time and keep the moisture. The maize needs two irrigations, some compound fertilizer at planting and urea at the big-flare stage, and about three sprays. I do not experiment with new crops at my age. Wheat and maize have buyers I know, prices I can predict, and my grandson can help me when the bags get heavy.
